items.title: Nolan took his cast out onto the open ocean and burned through two million feet of film, close to 380 miles of it, acros
items.summary:
Nolan took his cast out onto the open ocean and burned through two million feet of film, close to 380 miles of it, across 91 shooting days. The version where your chair fights back was mapped out afterward, by effects editors who normally get about two weeks per movie.

A 4DX chair moves three ways: it tips forward and back, swings side to side, and drops and lifts. That is all it can do. Everything else is vibration plus 21 environmental effects, including wind, water, fog, strobes, scent, and a jab to the shoulders that CJ 4DPlex staff have called the back kicker.

Your inner ear tracks how much you are really moving. Your eyes read the screen. When a ship pitches through a storm shot on IMAX film and your seat answers with a few inches of tilt, those two reports disagree, and the disagreement is the thing that turns your stomach. Researchers named it sensory conflict back in 1975. Three hours of small physical lies about a very large ocean.

4DX publishes its own list of people who should stay out of the chair: pregnant, elderly, prone to motion sickness, or living with high blood pressure, heart conditions, allergies, neck or back trouble, or epilepsy. The company warns its equipment can cause loss of balance, headaches, dizziness, and in rare cases epilepsy-like symptoms. Each seat is rated to hold 230 pounds. The tweet was a joke, but the list of people who should avoid the chair is the company's own.

Roughly 790 4DX rooms operate across about 70 countries. Only about 40 screens on earth can show The Odyssey the way it was shot, on IMAX 70mm film. One 4DX seat at Regal L.A. Live went for $36, and the equipment does not always work. A viewer asked for a refund after getting seat movement and nothing else, no wind and no water. Premium screens of every kind still took 52% of the film's $123.5 million opening weekend.

Adrian Ford, a Reddit reviewer who sits through nearly every 4DX release, bought tickets to both formats on opening weekend and checked the seating charts first. The IMAX house was sold out; the 4DX room had fewer than 20 people in it. Then videos like this one started circulating, and the comments underneath filled up with people asking which theater to book.
